name: Immunodeficiency with severe reduction in serum IgG and IgA with normal/elevated IgM and normal number of B-cells
aliases: Selective IgG and IgA deficiency with normal/elevated IgM

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Hyper IgM syndromes

criteria.description: Severe reduction in serum IgG and IgA levels
Normal or elevated serum IgM levels
History of recurrent bacterial infections, especially respiratory tract infections
Exclusion of other causes of hypogammaglobulinemia and immunodeficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe reduction in serum IgG and IgA with normal or elevated IgM and normal B-cell count, along with clinical history consistent with immunodeficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may confirm specific mutations associated with Hyper IgM syndromes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe hypogammaglobulinemia with absent IgG and IgA
searchTerms: very low IgG and IgA antibodies
absent major immunoglobulins IgG and IgA

pathognomonic.symptomName: Normal or elevated serum IgM concentration
searchTerms: normal or high IgM antibody levels
IgM levels within or above normal range
normal number of B cells in blood
failure to gain weight as baby
Cryptosporidium infection causing bile duct inflammation
intestinal parasite causing liver bile duct disease

laboratory: Severe reduction in serum IgG and IgA with normal or elevated IgM
Normal peripheral blood B-cell counts by flow cytometry
imaging: Chest X-ray showing recurrent or chronic pulmonary infections
Sinus CT scan demonstrating chronic sinusitis
genetic: Mutations in AICDA, UNG, or other genes associated with Hyper IgM syndrome type 3
other: Positive family history in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Reduced or absent CD40L expression on T-cells
Variable reduction in all immunoglobulin classes
Later onset compared to Hyper IgM syndrome

redFlags: Severe recurrent bacterial infections early in life
Failure to thrive despite adequate nutrition
Persistent hypogammaglobulinemia with normal B-cell counts
references: Notarangelo LD, et al. Hyper IgM syndromes: a model disease for studying defects in T cell help to B cells. Immunol Rev. 2005.

Orange JS, et al. Use and interpretation of diagnostic vaccination in primary immunodeficiency: a working group report of the Basic and Clinical Immunology Interest Section of the American Academy of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2012.
Picard C, et al. Clinical and immunological features of patients with activation-induced cytidine deaminase deficiency. Clin Immunol. 2006.
